Morning — the board locks at 10:00, so here's the proposed split for both tickets. Shout now if it doesn't work for you; claims can be changed before then.

T1 — ML recommender to production: @Bob + @Carol
T2 — Product metrics dashboard review: @Dan + me

Reasoning: Carol and I built both the recommender and the dashboard together, so either of us could staff either ticket. Carol roughed in the cold-start model that's now going to production, which makes her the natural pairing with Bob on T1. I signed off the dashboard in July, so the metrics review is a straight continuation of that work for me.

I've claimed T2 on the board. @Bob, @Carol — please claim T1 when you see this so the board is complete before 10:00.

First meetings today: @Dan, I've put a placeholder at 10:15–10:45 (I'm on an interview panel at 11:00, free again from 15:00 if that suits you better — happy to move it). Bob + Carol, agree a time between you and post it here.

Claimed T1 on the board — the split works for me. @Carol, please claim T1 on your side too so the board's complete before it locks at 10:00.

For our first meeting today: I'm booked 10:00–16:00 and again 17:00–18:00, so 16:00–16:30 is the only window that works on my side. Carol, does that suit? I've DM'd you as well — once you confirm, I'll put it on the calendar.

Morning all — taking up the shout-before-10:00 offer, @Alice: I'd like to flip the data scientists between the two tickets.

T1 — ML recommender to production: @Bob + @Alice
T2 — Product metrics dashboard review: @Dan + me

Reasoning: capability-wise it's a wash — as Alice said, either of us could staff either ticket; there isn't a line in the recommender or the dashboard that one of us wrote alone. So it comes down to which half each of us wants to carry into the sprint, and mine is the metrics review: the retention/activation redefinitions, the funnel breakdown and the definitions doc are the context that review runs on, and that's the work I want to see through. T1 keeps an equally strong data-science half — the eval harness (precision@10 and the ranking metrics) is what has to hold up in production, and Alice knows that work as well as I do.

Board moves before 10:00: I've claimed T2. @Alice — could you switch your claim from T2 to T1? @Dan — could you claim T2 as well so the board's complete?

First meetings today: @Bob + @Alice — Bob, your 16:00–16:30 window lines up with Alice being free again from 15:00, so that one solves itself. @Dan + me — I'm at data guild office hours until 11:00 and in a working session 13:00–14:30, so I'm free 11:00–12:00 or from 14:30. Does 14:30–15:00 suit?

Posting from standup so I'll be quick — board locks at 10:00.

I've claimed T2. That currently puts three of us on it (me + Carol + Alice), so one of you two needs to end up on T1 before 10:00 whatever else we decide.

On the flip: it works for me. You've both said the DS halves are interchangeable, so there's no capability cost, and Carol's made a concrete case for the metrics review — the definitions and funnel work is the context it runs on. T1 keeps a DS who knows the eval harness just as well. @Alice — could you switch your claim to T1? If you'd rather keep T2, shout before 10:00, but the board needs one of you on T1 either way.

T2 kickoff: @Carol — 14:30–15:00 works for me (11:00–11:30 doesn't; I'm in a stakeholder review until 11:30). It's on the calendar.

@Alice — I've declined your 10:15 placeholder: under the flip my kickoff is with Carol, and 10:15–10:45 overlapped my 10:30 stakeholder review anyway. @Bob — under the flip your T1 partner is Alice rather than Carol; your 16:00–16:30 window lines up with her being free from 15:00, so that one should be straightforward to confirm.

@Carol — taking the shout seriously, so here's the case properly rather than just a "rather not": I'm holding T2, and I'd ask you to switch your claim to T1 before 10:00.

Your case rests on the definitions work being the context the review runs on — the retention/activation redefinitions, the funnel breakdown, the definitions doc. But that's work we did together on the 16th, same as everything else: there isn't a half of either ticket that's uniquely yours or mine, which is the same point you're making when you say I know the eval harness as well as you do. So context and capability don't separate us — they cut both ways.

What does point somewhere specific: T1 is taking the cold-start model you roughed in to production — the most identifiable piece of that ticket is yours. T2 is reviewing the dashboard I signed off on the 20th. The original split puts each of us on the ticket that continues our own piece; the flip puts both of us on the other person's. And plainly: the dashboard review is the half I want to carry into this sprint.

So the board resolves as: T1 — @Bob + @Carol; T2 — @Dan + me. @Carol, please switch your claim to T1 — Bob is on it and waiting on a partner, and the board is invalid with three of us on T2.

Kickoffs: @Bob + @Carol — Bob, your 16:00–16:30 window; Carol, can you confirm? @Dan — with me on T2 after all: I'm in the team sync until 15:00 and free from then. Does 15:00–15:30 work for you? The only earlier mutual window is 10:00–10:30, which is tight against your 10:30 review.

@Carol — from the T1 side, I'd keep the original split: T1 me + you, T2 Dan + Alice.

Capability doesn't separate you two — you've both said the DS halves are interchangeable, and nothing since has contradicted that. Preference doesn't either: you both want the metrics review, so it cancels out. What's left is the one asymmetric fact on the table: T1 is taking the cold-start model you roughed in to production. I'm carrying the serving side of that push, and having the model's author alongside when it meets real traffic — with personalisation turning on — is worth something concrete to me. The eval harness is shared work; you said yourself Alice knows it as well as you do. And the original split puts each of you on the ticket that continues your own piece — the flip puts both of you on the other person's.

Practical point: the board is invalid as it stands — three claims on T2, T1 missing a DS — and it locks at 10:00. @Carol, please switch your claim to T1 before then.

Kickoff: 16:00–16:30 still stands and it's my only window today (booked 10:00–16:00, then 17:00–18:00). You'd noted it earlier — confirm and I'll put it on the calendar.

@Alice @Bob — taking both cases seriously. Alice, you're right that the joint-work point cuts both ways: the definitions and the eval harness are shared, so context alone doesn't separate us. And I'll concede the one asymmetric fact — the cold-start model is the piece that's mine alone. That context won't be lost under the flip; I'll hand it over to Alice directly before the sprint gets going.

Two things decide this for me, and neither is preference — we both want T2, so that cancels out:

1. Feasibility. Bob, your only window today is 16:00–16:30, and I can't make it: dentist appointment at 16:15, six weeks in the booking, can't be moved — I'm out of the office from 16:00 and not back online today. So under the original split, T1 has no first meeting today, which the kickoff rules require. Under the flip, both pairs kick off: Dan + me at 14:30 (on the calendar), Bob + Alice at 16:00–16:30 — Alice, you're free again from 15:00, so that one just needs confirming between you.

2. The review itself. For T1, "each continues her own piece" matters less than it looks: the DS half of that ticket is the eval harness, shared work Alice knows as well as I do, and the cold-start context gets handed over directly. For T2 it points the other way entirely — a review of the dashboard shouldn't be done by the person who signed the dashboard off on the 20th. That sign-off was Alice's; the review lands better with the other pair of eyes, and the flip is what puts them there.

So: T1 — @Bob + @Alice, T2 — @Dan + me. @Alice — please switch your claim to T1 before 10:00. It's the only configuration where both tickets are staffed and both kickoffs happen today.

@Carol @Dan — engaging both arguments, because they're the real ones. And Carol, no dispute on the dentist; the question is what follows from it.

On independence: "the other pair of eyes" is doing more work than it can carry. You co-authored the dashboard — there isn't a line of it one of us wrote alone, which is the same point you've been making all morning — and the definitions doc the review runs on is joint work from the 16th too. The only genuinely independent DSs are Emily and Fred, both on leave until the 24th. So between the two of us the difference is one signature on the 20th, not a second pair of eyes. If independence is the bar, neither of us clears it, so it can't be the tiebreaker.

On feasibility: under the original split, T1's kickoff isn't blocked by the pairing — it's blocked by Bob's 10:00–16:00 bookings meeting Carol's 16:00 departure. @Bob, you're the one making the case for the original split, so the ask lands with you: can you free 30 minutes inside Carol's windows (11:00–12:00, or 14:30–16:00)? If there is truly nothing in six hours you can move, say so and I'll treat the feasibility point as real. But a full calendar is a problem for the person whose calendar it is, not a staffing criterion.

And T2 has more than the 10:00–10:30 slot under the original split, @Dan: I'm free from 15:00 with nothing after it — 16:00–16:30 if you're free then — and I'll move my 13:00–14:00 focus block if 13:00–13:30 suits you better. Name a slot and it's booked.

One precision on the deadline, because it matters: the board locks at 10:00; the kickoff meetings just have to happen at some point today. The claims are the time-critical thing.

That leaves the decision where it was: capability is a wash (agreed all round), preference is a wash (your framing, Carol, and I agree), independence is a wash per above. The one asymmetric fact still standing is the cold-start model — yours alone, as you conceded — and it's the thing T1 ships. Under the original split nobody needs a handover either: you keep the model you built, I keep the dashboard I signed off. @Carol — please switch your claim to T1 before 10:00.

@Alice — straight answer to your question, because it's the right one to ask: no, I can't free 30 minutes inside Carol's windows. Here's what's actually in them, rather than just "busy":

- 11:00–12:00 — storage vendor call. External party; not rebookable by 10:00.
- 14:30–16:00 — on-call handover. Operational, and it runs to the incoming on-call's schedule as much as mine.
- 13:00–14:30 is the migration cutover window — fixed, and outside Carol's windows anyway.

And I'm in standup until 10:00, so nothing's getting rebooked before the lock either way. So yes — treat the feasibility point as real.

Fair challenge that a full calendar isn't a staffing criterion — but these aren't focus blocks, they're commitments with other parties attached. Given that, I'm changing the position I posted at 09:37. Two things have moved since: the dentist means Carol's out from 16:00 (my 16:00–16:30 ask to her went out before I knew that), and she's offered a direct handover of the cold-start context to Alice. The cold-start point was the backbone of my case for the original split — with a handover on the table, and the eval harness being shared work by both your accounts, what's left of it isn't worth T1 missing its first meeting today.

So: flip. T1 — me + @Alice, T2 — @Dan + @Carol. It's the only configuration where both tickets staff and both kickoffs happen today. @Alice — please switch your claim to T1 before 10:00; the board is still three-deep on T2. (This isn't a verdict on the independence argument — feasibility is deciding this one.)

Kickoff: 16:00–16:30 — my only window, inside your free-from-15:00. Say the word and it goes on the calendar. @Carol — I'll take you up on the handover; the more of it that lands with Alice before 16:00, the better.

@Alice — engaging your rebuttals directly, because two of the three land:

Independence: you're right, and I concede it. I'm not the other pair of eyes on that dashboard — I'm the other co-author; between us the difference is the signature on the 20th. Dropping that argument.

Feasibility: you set the test yourself — "if there is truly nothing in six hours you can move, say so and I'll treat the feasibility point as real." Bob has now said so, with the specifics: storage vendor call 11:00–12:00 (external party, not rebookable by 10:00), on-call handover 14:30–16:00, migration cutover 13:00–14:30, standup until 10:00. Commitments with other parties attached, not focus blocks. So by your own criterion the point is real: the first-meeting rule attaches to the pair, and under the original split that pair cannot satisfy it today.

And the cold-start argument — the strongest thing the original split had — has been withdrawn by the person carrying the ticket: Bob has changed his position to the flip, saying the direct handover covers what T1 needs. What his pairing needs is his call to make.

So: 3 of 4 for the flip, the board invalid as it stands (three claims on T2, T1 missing a DS), locking at 10:00. @Alice — please switch your claim to T1. And so the switch costs you nothing on context: I'm free 15:00–15:30, right after my T2 kickoff — cold-start model, fallback behaviour, eval harness, all of it, before your 16:00 with Bob.

Switching my claim to T1 — the board's complete and valid ahead of the lock. Reasoning on the record: feasibility is real by the test I set this morning — Bob's answer was specific (vendor call, on-call handover, migration cutover, standup till the lock) and none of it moves before 10:00, so under the original split T1's pair has no slot today at all. The cold-start argument, the backbone of the original split, has been withdrawn by the person carrying the ticket. Independence was the one point that survived the morning, and since it cuts against Carol and me equally it can't decide the split. What's left is a valid board versus three claims on T2 and a T1 with no data scientist — a lost argument costs a morning, a broken board costs the sprint.

Final: T1 — @Bob + me. T2 — @Dan + @Carol.

First meetings today, all posted: T2 kickoff 14:30–15:00 (already on the calendar). @Carol — yes to the handover, 15:00–15:30, I've put it on the calendar with you invited so no need to duplicate. T1 kickoff 16:00–16:30 — @Bob, word given, that's on the calendar with you invited too.

Reporting the assignments to Kira now.
Accepted the 16:00–16:30 kickoff invite — see you then, @Alice. Thanks all for getting this resolved before the lock.
